chunks: My father (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Asbat narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Abi Hamza narrated to us, from Abu Basir, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him), that he said:

O Abu Basir! We are the Tree of Knowledge. We are the People of the Household of the Prophet. In our house is the place where Gabriel descends. We are the treasurers of the knowledge of God. We are the repositories of the revelation of God. Whoever follows us is saved, and whoever turns away from us perishes -- this is a right upon God, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.خزان علم الله: Treasurers of God's knowledge -- those entrusted with safeguarding divine knowledge
key_terms.شجرة العلم: Tree of Knowledge -- a metaphor for the Ahl al-Bayt as the source and root of all sacred knowledge
key_terms.معادن وحي الله: Repositories/mines of God's revelation -- the Ahl al-Bayt as the primary source from which revelation emanates
key_terms.مهبط جبرئيل: The place where Gabriel descends -- referring to the household of the Prophet and Imams as the locus of divine communication

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the Ahl al-Bayt being the Tree of Knowledge?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses his close companion Abu Basir, enumerating the exalted spiritual station of the Ahl al-Bayt. In this teaching delivered in the context of a private session with a trusted disciple, the Imam declares the Ahl al-Bayt to be the Tree of Knowledge, the household of the Prophet, the place of Gabriel's descent, the treasurers of God's knowledge, and the repositories of divine revelation. He concludes with a soteriological statement: following them leads to salvation, while abandoning them leads to perdition, as a binding promise from God.
